article.Citation/Title: Pagni, B. A., Petridis, P. D., Podrebarac, S. K., Grinband, J., Claus, E. D., & Bogenschutz, M. P. (2024). Psilocybin-induced changes in neural reactivity to alcohol and emotional cues in patients with alcohol use disorder: an fMRI pilot study. Scientific Reports, 14, 3159.
article.Outcome: Alcohol-cue treatment-by-time interaction: 8 activation + 17 deactivation clusters, whole-brain (psilocybin vs placebo, p-unc<.005, k=10)
article.InterventionDescription: Psilocybin 25 mg/70 kg (n=5) vs diphenhydramine 50 mg placebo (n=6), single oral dose, 8-h monitored session; preceded by 4 prep therapy sessions

article.Citation/Title: This is a secondary/ancillary fMRI analysis of participants drawn from the parent phase II RCT: Bogenschutz, M. P. et al. (2022), 'Percentage of Heavy Drinking Days Following Psilocybin-Assisted Psychotherapy vs Placebo in the Treatment of Adult Patients With Alcohol Use Disorder: A Randomized Clinical Trial,' JAMA Psychiatry (NCT02061293, ref. 16 in this article). Fourteen of the parent trial's participants consented to this ancillary fMRI sub-study; 11 provided complete pre/post scan data and are analyzed here. Eligible per the secondary-analysis boundary case.
article.EligibleYN: (a) Clinical trial: satisfied via the secondary-analysis boundary case — participants were randomized within the parent RCT protocol (psilocybin vs diphenhydramine) with prospectively planned fMRI outcome assessment; this is not a retrospective or naturalistic study. (b) SUD-related outcome: satisfied by the Craving data section, which reports pre-to-post psilocybin-group reduction in cue-elicited craving ratings (t(3)=5.568, p=0.0114) — craving is an explicitly listed qualifying SUD outcome. Both criteria met, so EligibleYN=Y even though the article's own stated primary outcome is neural reactivity, not drinking or craving.
article.Outcome: Abstract and Results state the study's aim/primary outcome is psilocybin-induced neural reactivity to alcohol (and emotional) cues, not a drinking or craving endpoint — this is a genuine primary-outcome/SUD-outcome discrepancy (craving is secondary here; see EligibleYN and Pos Result Y/N notes). The alcohol-cue task is listed and reported first among the three cue types and matches the article's title, so it is treated as the primary comparison (Results 'Alcohol cue neural reactivity', Table 2). The analysis is a whole-brain voxelwise treatment-by-time interaction yielding many discrete significant clusters (8 activation, 17 deactivation; Table 2) rather than one scalar primary effect size, so a single number would misrepresent the design. Coded as a short labelled descriptor rather than picking one cluster, which would arbitrarily privilege that cluster over dozens of co-equal exploratory findings and bias interpretation.
article.SD: No single paired dispersion/test statistic exists for a whole-brain cluster map: Table 2 reports per-cluster voxel extents and cluster-/peak-level p-values individually (e.g., L MFG activation cluster: 188 voxels, cluster p-unc=0.002, peak p-unc<0.001). Coded '.' because pairing one cluster's statistic with the Outcome descriptor (which spans all 8+17 clusters) would misrepresent a single-cluster value as representative of the whole finding.
article.PVal: The uniform whole-brain statistical threshold applied to define significant clusters for the alcohol-cue treatment-by-time interaction was p-uncorrected < 0.005 (k=10 voxel extent), stated in Methods ('fMRI modeling and analyses') and used consistently in Table 2. Reported as the threshold string exactly as used, since no single omnibus p-value applies to the composite multi-cluster Outcome.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: Eleven participants (psilocybin n=5, placebo n=6) comprised the final analyzed fMRI sample after excluding 3 of the original 14 ancillary-study enrollees (2 did not complete both visits; 1 had fMRI malfunction at the pre-intervention visit) — Results, 'Demographics'. This N=11 is the denominator for all cue-reactivity results in Tables 2-4, including the alcohol-cue Outcome.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: Boundary call, flagged for review: n_met=13/14, the exact threshold for MethodologyDescribedYN=1. 'harms' is the sole unmet criterion — this article never mentions adverse events, harms, or safety in any form (not even 'not assessed here'), so it cannot be credited as 'described.' 'sample_size_power' was credited Y because the Limitations section explicitly states the small sample size 'restricts generalizations and limits statistical power,' mirroring the Power field's own convention that a bare underpowered statement counts as discussed; no a priori power calculation is reported. If a reviewer instead requires an a priori justification for sample_size_power, n_met=12 and the binary flips to 0 — the single closest call in this record. 'setting' credited Y on the basis of named research institutions/scanner facility (NYU Langone; CBI Siemens Skyra) rather than an explicit clinical-setting descriptor (e.g., 'outpatient').

article.Pos Result Y/N: Directionally mixed but net-positive per the authors' own interpretation: increased PFC/caudate engagement and decreased insula/motor/cerebellar activity are framed throughout Discussion/Conclusion as consistent with 'potential therapeutic neural changes' and 'encouraging' findings, and the one clean behavioral statistic reported (psilocybin-group craving reduction, t(3)=5.568, p=0.0114) was significant and positive. Not coded 3 despite some caveated directionality (e.g., mPFC increases framed as possibly inconsistent with simple 'normalization') because the authors do not describe the overall result as ambiguous or mixed — they consistently characterize it as therapeutically promising.
article.Retention (%): 14 participants were randomized into the ancillary fMRI sub-study (psilocybin n=6, placebo n=8; Methods, 'Parent trial and fMRI sub-study'); 11 completed both scans and are analyzed (psilocybin n=5, placebo n=6). Retention = 11/14 x 100 = 78.57%, within 2 points of the 80% cutoff — flagged per instructions since this is close enough to flip a downstream quality cell.
article.Comparator: Comparator is diphenhydramine 50 mg, described as an 'active placebo' matched to maintain blinding (mimics some subjective/somatic effects without psychoactivity), administered under identical session structure to psilocybin. Coded 1 as an active comparator, not an inert placebo.
article.BaseStatus: No AUD severity classification (e.g., number of DSM criteria met, mild/moderate/severe specifier) is reported anywhere in this article; only baseline drinking quantity/frequency and craving descriptives are given (Table 1). Coded '.' — the concept applies but was not reported in this article.
article.Age_Median: Weighted sample mean age = (48.80x5 + 44.00x6)/11 = 46.18 years (Table 1, psilocybin and placebo group means), falling in the 30-50 bracket.
article.PercentFem: Sample size (male/female): psilocybin 5 (4/1), placebo 6 (3/3) — Table 1. Female = 1+3 = 4 of 11 = 36.36%.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: Table 1 race/ethnicity: psilocybin White(4), Hispanic(1); placebo White(4), Hispanic(1), Black(1); total N=11 (8+2+1=11, consistent with sample size). As tabulated, 'White' and 'Hispanic' are presented as separate, non-overlapping categories, so non-white/BIPOC = Hispanic(2) + Black(1) = 3/11 = 27.27%. Flagging the standard ambiguity that Hispanic/Latino ethnicity can cross racial categories elsewhere in the literature; here the source table treats it as mutually exclusive from White, and that convention was followed as-reported.
article.SocioeconomicStatusYN: Annual income is reported by group (psilocybin $97,500; placebo $148,333; Table 1), but the Limitations section explicitly characterizes the sample as 'of middle-to-high socioeconomic status' with no low-income eligibility pathway or public-insurance criterion described. Coded 0 because the field asks whether low-SES participants were explicitly included/described, not merely whether income was reported.
article.Country_USvsNonUS: All sites are in the United States (NYU Langone/NYU Grossman School of Medicine, New York, NY; Columbia University imaging center; Penn State co-author affiliation) — Methods and author affiliations.
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: Limitations explicitly states the sample was 'nondiverse, homogeneous... primarily Caucasian, of young adult age, and of middle-to-high socioeconomic status,' and participants were drawn from a screened phase II RCT (SCID-confirmed AUD, extensive exclusion criteria) rather than a real-world/community-representative sample.
article.ConfoundYN: Baseline group differences were formally tested (t-tests/chi-squared across sex, age, weight, craving, PHDD, DPD, PDD, framewise displacement; Table 1), one of which (PDD) differed significantly and is discussed as a caveat. Six realignment (motion) parameters were entered as covariates in first-level fMRI models. Age, sex, and smoking status are explicitly flagged in Limitations as unaddressed potential confounds. Coded 1 for substantive assessment/discussion, even though full statistical adjustment for demographic confounds was not performed (small-sample degrees-of-freedom limitation, noted in Limitations).
article.Followup in months: This article's own post-treatment assessment window is the second fMRI scan, obtained a mean of 1.45 days (SD=0.68, range 1-3) after the first drug administration (Results, 'Demographics') — there is no longer-horizon follow-up reported in this article itself. Converted 1.45 days / 30 = 0.048, rounded to 0.05 months. Note this is far shorter than the parent trial's own primary-outcome follow-up (8 months post-treatment, ref. 16), which is not part of this article's reported analyses.
article.SafetyReported: This article contains no Adverse Events, Safety, or Side-effects section, table, or sentence of any kind — it is a neuroimaging mechanism paper; harms/safety reporting for this cohort appears to live in the parent trial publication (ref. 16), not here. Coded SafetyReported=N per the 'article silent on AEs/safety entirely' convention, cascading AnyAEReported/NumDistinctAEs/NParticipantsWithAE=NA, AE_denominator='.', ArmScope=NA, WorstSeverity=NA, and ae_events=[].
article.HarmsAssessed: Coded 0 to agree with SafetyReported=N per the required HarmsAssessed/SafetyReported concordance rule; this article does not state whether harms were or were not assessed for this fMRI sub-sample.

config_proposal.metric: Whole-brain fMRI cluster-level statistics (multiple discrete clusters comprising the primary outcome; no single scalar effect size)
config_proposal.note: The primary outcome is a whole-brain voxelwise neuroimaging analysis reporting many discrete significant clusters (8 activation + 17 deactivation for the alcohol-cue interaction alone; more for the emotional-cue tasks) rather than one pooled between-group scalar statistic. No defensible single-number Hedges' g (or other supported-method) conversion exists without arbitrarily privileging one cluster over dozens of co-equal exploratory findings, so this is excluded from Tier 1 and routed to Tier 2 qualitative classification instead.
config_proposal.tier2_basis: Significant reduction in psilocybin-group cue-elicited craving post-treatment (t(3)=5.568, p=0.0114) plus multiple significant whole-brain treatment-by-time interaction clusters in the direction the authors interpret as therapeutic (increased PFC/caudate engagement, decreased insula/motor/cerebellar activity), tempered by the very small pilot sample (n=11), uncorrected p<.005 whole-brain threshold, and the authors' own caution that some directionality is not straightforwardly consistent with AUD-circuit normalization.
